core_process.explanation: Linguists encounter openness through peers, supervisors, libraries, open-source communities, workshops, teaching, and direct exchange. They assemble linked records of manuscripts, data, code, materials, versions, annotation decisions, and processing information, calibrating disclosure to consent, copyright, identifiability, participant acceptability, evidentiary needs, and the situated production of data. Whether this becomes routine depends on practical capability, discoverable infrastructure, equitable access routes, workflow timing, governance administration, career and scrutiny risks, and whether requirements are accompanied by funding, guidance, recognition, and collaboration.
core_process.name: Assembling claim-adequate, interpretable access through supported and governance-aware practice

incidents.action_or_process: Constructing and maintaining a connected record beyond the final article.
incidents.meaning: Openness entails publications, data, code, tools, procedures, versions, annotation documentation, and identifiable links whose components can be found and understood.
incidents.open_code: Constructing a traceable, linked, discoverable, and interpretable research record

incidents.action_or_process: Framing openness for research, education, and public use without imposing one label.
incidents.meaning: Science, research, scholarship, and education are pragmatically delimited across disciplinary and linguistic identities; educational and public audiences may need distinct resources or presentations.
incidents.open_code: Negotiating openness labels and intended audiences

incidents.action_or_process: Separating shareable methods, materials, metadata, derived evidence, and access routes from restricted primary data.
incidents.meaning: Researchers disclose the most useful permissible full, partial, derived, delayed, or mediated evidence while documenting consent, privacy, copyright, identifiability, selection, and data-collection conditions.
incidents.open_code: Calibrating claim-adequate disclosure to governed and situated language data

incidents.action_or_process: Learning and trying open practices through situated models, dialogue, and hands-on support.
incidents.meaning: Awareness, consumption, contribution, teaching, and advocacy remain distinct. Movement is supported through open-source communities, peers, supervisors, libraries, workshops, direct exchange, teaching, and visible examples, but exposure alone does not assure contribution.
incidents.open_code: Developing participation through practical communities and early collaborative learning

incidents.action_or_process: Aligning requirements, access infrastructure, support, visibility, and evaluation with open practice.
incidents.meaning: Journals, funders, institutions, repositories, libraries, and teaching programs can normalize openness through claim-relevant expectations, accessible publishing routes, financial and technical support, and recognition; mandates without these arrangements can alienate or exclude.
incidents.open_code: Embedding supported, equitable, and incentive-aligned accountability

incidents.action_or_process: Sequencing, limiting, standardizing, or integrating disclosure and governance work under competing demands.
incidents.meaning: Preparation, anonymization, repository review, permissions, archiving, legal uncertainty, priority, criticism, and career arrangements shape whether disclosure is timely and extensive.
incidents.open_code: Negotiating labour, administrative governance, priority, credit, and scrutiny

incidents.action_or_process: Opening sufficient evidence and decision trails for checking, replication, and reflexive interpretation.
incidents.meaning: Open materials can enable evaluation, correction, replication, reanalysis, and learning, but qualitative and mixed linguistic work also requires an account of annotation, selection, researcher position, and mediation rather than treating data as self-explanatory.
incidents.open_code: Making claims technically reviewable and interpretively accountable

incidents.action_or_process: Sharing, attributing, adapting, translating, and extending materials for diverse users.
incidents.meaning: Open outputs can reduce dependency on privileged networks and support research, teaching, public learning, and collaborative extension when they are attributable, intelligible, lawful, and responsive to intended users.
incidents.open_code: Redistributing access through attributed reuse, translation, and collaborative extension

memos.analytic_decision: Retain the record category but expand it to interpretable availability; redefine reviewability as technical and interpretive accountability, allowing bounded replication without original raw data.
memos.observation: New accounts distinguish records from files, usable data from non-machine-readable appendices, and full data access from replication based on a well-described method. Qualitative work adds annotation and positional decision trails.
memos.title: Memo: A deposited record is not necessarily usable evidence
memos.uncertainty: The corpus does not establish what degree of methodological detail, metadata, or access is sufficient for different linguistic designs.

memos.analytic_decision: Refine labour into labour-and-governance negotiation and retain conditional disclosure as distinct from noncompliance; treat standardized guidance as a potentially enabling form of support.
memos.observation: Anonymization, permissions, participant reluctance, and detailed institutional applications consume time before material can be shared. Funding and policies do not by themselves make these processes workable.
memos.title: Memo: Governance work is a constitutive condition, not merely a legal exception
memos.uncertainty: The interviews do not show which standardized procedures protect participants while reducing burden across data types and jurisdictions.

memos.analytic_decision: Broaden the core process from assembling accessible materials to assembling claim-adequate and interpretively accountable access, and retain practical dialogue as a participation pathway.
memos.observation: A26 treats annotation manuals, researcher position, and mediated collection as what openness should reveal; A24 shows replication can be learned through explicit description and comparative inquiry.
memos.title: Memo: Openness exposes situated interpretation
memos.uncertainty: It remains unclear how researchers can document positionality and collaborative interpretation without creating new burdens or falsely implying that all interpretations are commensurable.

propositions.statement: When openness is organized as a linked, discoverable, and interpretable research record rather than as free publication or an isolated deposit, participants include files, identifiable versions, connections, and decision documentation needed to find and assess what was done.

Disclosure is more likely to support evaluation and replication when it is claim-adequate and situated: researchers provide the most useful permissible primary, partial, derived, or mediated materials and document restrictions and relevant decisions.

Situated exposure can support movement from awareness toward contribution when it supplies practical models, direct exchange, and accessible support, but attendance, endorsement, or consumption alone does not establish routine contribution.

Institutional requirements are more likely to make openness practicable when paired with financial, technical, legal, and discoverability support and with career recognition; unsupported requirements or inaccessible routes can add burden, demotivate, or reproduce unequal access.

Where cleaning, anonymization, repository curation, permissions, priority concerns, criticism, and publication pressure remain individualized, researchers may favor delayed, restricted, or minimum-compliance disclosure even while valuing openness.

Open access can broaden reciprocal research, educational, and public learning when outputs are attributable, findable, intelligible, and usable by intended audiences; access alone does not ensure equitable reach or collaborative extension.

relationships.explanation: Supervisors, peers, libraries, open-source communities, workshops, and direct exchanges provide models and skills for constructing interpretable records.
Accessible support, teaching, and institutional arrangements can extend participation beyond already interested attendees.
Consent, copyright, participant concerns, and the situated production of language data determine whether records contain primary data, derived evidence, or mediated access routes.
Cleaning, anonymization, permissions, repository review, and administrative applications limit the scope and timing of record construction.
Claim-relevant expectations, accessible publishing routes, repositories, and support make review materials and decision trails more feasible.
Reviewability makes a record consequential by enabling inspection, correction, bounded replication, and scrutiny of technical and interpretive decisions.
Findable, interpretable records supply material that can be attributed, reused, translated, and collaboratively extended.
When permissions and curation are individualized extra work, requirements need standardized guidance, time, funding, and recognition to remain practicable.

theoretical_sampling_questions.evidence_gap: The corpus contains contrasting expectations about mandates but few matched cases across institutions with different funding, legal help, repository support, and promotion criteria.
theoretical_sampling_questions.question: When do mandatory disclosure policies produce sustained, claim-adequate sharing rather than minimum-compliance or demotivation?
theoretical_sampling_questions.suggested_next_cases_or_data: Sample researchers subject to similar mandates in institutions with and without APC funding, data stewards, legal consultation, and career credit; compare deposited records, timing, restrictions, and accounts of burden.

theoretical_sampling_questions.evidence_gap: Participants propose transcripts, measurements, excerpts, request access, and documentation, but the corpus rarely follows these arrangements through actual reanalysis.
theoretical_sampling_questions.question: Which forms of mediated disclosure permit meaningful scrutiny of sensitive speech, video, clinical, classroom, and copyrighted corpus research?
theoretical_sampling_questions.suggested_next_cases_or_data: Sample completed projects using each access model and interview depositors, data-access committees, and reusers; inspect whether a qualified outsider can assess the stated claim and where the process fails.

theoretical_sampling_questions.evidence_gap: Many pathways to awareness are described, but sustained practice after exposure is uneven and under-observed.
theoretical_sampling_questions.question: What converts workshop, library, peer, or supervisor exposure into routine contribution rather than one-time awareness or consumption?
theoretical_sampling_questions.suggested_next_cases_or_data: Follow novice researchers before and after practical workshops, mentorship, or project onboarding; compare participants who later deposit, document, teach, or advocate with those who do not.

theoretical_sampling_questions.evidence_gap: The corpus distinguishes deposit from findability and reports opaque platforms, but provides little observation of search and reuse behavior.
theoretical_sampling_questions.question: How do discoverability, metadata, repository design, and stable versioning affect whether deposited linguistic materials are found and reused?
theoretical_sampling_questions.suggested_next_cases_or_data: Sample repositories and records with differing metadata, identifiers, linking, and access rules; conduct task-based searches with researchers, teachers, and students and trace actual reuse or abandonment.

theoretical_sampling_questions.evidence_gap: Fear of criticism is prominent, while observed cases of supportive correction are comparatively few.
theoretical_sampling_questions.question: Under what conditions does scrutiny become constructive correction rather than feared career exposure or silence?
theoretical_sampling_questions.suggested_next_cases_or_data: Sample cases of public code/data review, replication, correction notices, and open versus anonymous review across career stages; compare attribution, tone, consequences, and subsequent sharing behavior.
